methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $3.3B - $7.6B.

private.name: Archer Aviation
private.rationale: Same sector (Drones & Autonomous), same stage (Public), post-money $3.33B

data.narrative:
Joby Aviation, a public-stage drone and autonomous systems company, is evaluated against a peer set of three same-sector comparables spanning Series G private and public-stage companies. The broader universe encompasses seven private frontier-tech peers in drones and autonomous systems, including Archer Aviation, Zipline, and Nuro.

The peer-median method anchors valuation analysis. Three comparable companies—Zipline ($7.6B Series G), Nuro ($6.0B Series G), and Archer Aviation ($3.3B public)—yield a median valuation of $6.0B, with a range spanning $3.3B to $7.6B. This peer-median approach directly implies a $6.0B valuation for Joby.

Triangulation across available methods supports a valuation range of $5.1B to $6.9B, with a median of $6.0B. Joby's current public valuation of $6.86B falls within the upper end of this derived range, approximately 14% above the peer median. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three-company peer set and stage-specific valuation multiples, given the mix of private Series G and public comparables. The narrow peer count limits the robustness of the median estimate; expansion to additional same-stage public companies or growth-stage private peers would refine conviction in the range.
